regressions.source: StUsds.sol permit(..., bytes signature): require(_isValidSignature(owner, digest, signature), 'StUsds/invalid-permit'); allowance[owner][spender] = value; emit Approval(owner, spender, value);
regressions.issue: The free-pointer bump of the returned-bytes allocation is now kept (correct), which makes mem[64] a join value after the if. Then the Approval value prints as raw memory instead of amount, and the 'StUsds/invalid-permit' revert as hex words plus 'revert with memory'. The success path is nested in 'if _59: ... stop' with the revert after it. _62 and _64 are each a load of mem[64] with no store before the use, so '_62 - mem[64]' is 0.
regressions.rule: Two loads of mem[64] with no store to mem[64] between them are one value, also when mem[64] is a join value (fold _62 - mem[64] to 0). Then mem[p len 32] just written resolves, and the Error(string) revert prints its message.

notes: Diff of 76 lines, read in full. The other 'StUsds/invalid-permit' reverts of the function are still decoded (4 -> 3 decoded). The v,r,s permit has the same ERC-1271 tail but is unchanged apart from the constant. The rewritten copy bound and the zero store after the copy (2 * _38 - _44 + 2 * Mask(250, 5, signature.length + 31) + 32) equal the old _47-based forms. Same root cause as c00040/c00149/c00173/c00019: the free pointer is not kept exact across a join, and equal mem[64] loads are not merged.
